# CXNM - Standard - AND - U - Compliance Corporate Defender for Endpoint

Marks a fully managed or corporate-owned Android device as non-compliant when Defender for Endpoint gives it a risk score higher than low.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Android |
| Scope | User (U) — assign to user groups |
| Type | Compliance |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | UniFy Android Enterprise Baseline v1.5.1 — AND - CP - DEV - Defender - Corp-Devices - v1.5; compared with IntuneAdmin Baseline - Android Enterprise - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (level medium) |
| File | [`Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Corporate_Defender_for_Endpoint.json`](Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Corporate_Defender_for_Endpoint.json) |

> Three prerequisites, otherwise every device is non-compliant or nothing is measured: (1) a licence for Defender for Endpoint (P1/P2, Business, or Microsoft 365 E5/Business Premium); (2) the Defender–Intune connector enabled, with *Connect Android devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint* set to On; (3) the Microsoft Defender app (`com.microsoft.scmx`) deployed as a required Managed Google Play app, preferably with the app configuration in extras/android/app-configuration so that onboarding happens without user action. Deliberately a separate policy and not in Device Health: that way you can assign it only once the connector is in place, and a missing licence stays limited to this one check. There is no overlap: the Device Health policies leave `deviceThreatProtectionEnabled` at false, which in compliance means "not required" — no conflict. Anyone using a different Mobile Threat Defense partner sets `deviceThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` instead of `advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel`.

| CA policy | State | What this policy does for it |
|---|---|---|
| [2060 - GRANT - Mobile Apps and Desktop Clients](https://github.com/ConXioN-ITCE/CIPP-Templates-ConditionalAccess/blob/main/CATemplate/CXNM__STANDARD__2060__GRANT__Mobile_Apps_and_Desktop_Clients.en.md) | disabled | Helps determine whether a device is compliant. If a device fails it, the device becomes non-compliant and the compliant-device requirement in Conditional Access stops it. |

## Properties — 9

A compliance policy has no settingDefinitionIds but fixed properties. `scheduledActionsForRule` determines what happens when a device does not comply.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| `deviceThreatProtectionEnabled` | true |
| `deviceThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` | unavailable |
| `advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` | low |
| `scheduledActionsForRule[0].ruleName` | PasswordRequired |
| `scheduledActionsForRule[0].scheduledActionConfigurations[0].@odata.type` | #microsoft.graph.deviceComplianceActionItem |
| `scheduledActionsForRule[0].scheduledActionConfigurations[0].gracePeriodHours` | 24 |
| `scheduledActionsForRule[0].scheduledActionConfigurations[0].actionType` | block |
| `scheduledActionsForRule[0].scheduledActionConfigurations[0].notificationTemplateId` | 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 |
| `scheduledActionsForRule[0].scheduledActionConfigurations[0].notificationMessageCCList` | — |
